subject: Post-call: Dedicated perf validation hypothesis + next steps
messages:
From: Jordan Li <jordan.li@acmehealth.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-20T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Thanks + perf targets we discussed

Hi Priya,

Thanks again for walking through Redwood's hosting and Dedicated options today — that was helpful. Quick recap from our side and a few asks so we can scope the pilot: 

Summary of our requirements (from the call):
- Model: fine-tuned LlamaR-13B (~7.5B effective after pruning), typical prompt+generation length ~512 tokens (avg), peak up to 1024.
- Latency SLO: p95 <= 120ms for non-streaming generation at 512 tokens; for streaming use-cases we need partial tokens delivered within 60ms of generation for first partial and consistent 40-80ms thereafter.
- Throughput: steady-state 10 req/s sustained per reserved pool (with periodic bursts to 25 req/s for 2-5 minutes).
- Concurrency: average 8 concurrent sessions; occasional spikes to ~30 concurrent.
- Availability: warm KV cache is important; we expect many short-turn requests.

Can you confirm the test matrix you recommend (GPU candidates, perf harness, warmup window, batch/concurrency knobs) and a proposed 2-week pilot calendar? I've attached a small telemetry snapshot from our production traffic (acme_prod_profile.csv) that shows token distribution and burst patterns.

Also, can you include a short note about expected reserved throughput sizing across H100 / A100 / L4 options — we want to compare cost and headroom.

Jordan
Jordan Li
Head of Platform, Acme Health
ops@acmehealth.com

Attachment: acme_prod_profile.csv (CSV, 42KB)
From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Li <jordan.li@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-21T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Thanks + perf targets we discussed

Jordan — thanks for the clear recap and the telemetry file. This is exactly what we need to size a concise pilot. High-level proposal and next steps below.

Short proposal (TL;DR):
- Pilot: 2-week dedicated validation run in a Reserved pool. Objective: validate p95 latency target at 512 tokens, streaming partial latency envelope, and sustained 10 req/s throughput with headroom for bursts to 25 req/s.
- GPUs to test: H100 80GB (fp8/ampere-like kernel), A100 80GB, and L4 (cost-efficient, quantized path). We'll produce a head-to-head matrix of latency/throughput/cost-per-token.
- Reserved throughput guidance: start with a reserved throughput of 12 req/s (provides ~20% headroom for steady state) and allow autoscaling bursts up to 30 req/s for 5-minute windows during the pilot.
- Concurrency & batching: target 8 concurrent sessions in steady state with an aggressive batch window (5-10ms) for latency-sensitive routes; for streaming routes disable large batch accumulation and use continuous-kv-path.
- Warm-up: 30-minute warm-up with synthetic traces matched to your token-distribution (thank you for the CSV). We'll also run a rolling-cold-warm stress to see cold-cache tail effects.

Deliverables during pilot:
- Daily perf dashboard (p50/p95/p99, per-route token cost, token/sec).
- Side-by-side GPU matrix with expected cost per 1M tokens.
- A short ops runbook: warmup steps, autoscale knobs, recommended quantization profile if L4 needed.

Action items for both sides: 
1) You: confirm test window (we propose 7/5 - 7/19) and provide a point of contact for SRE and Procurement.
2) Redwood (Ben/Karthik/Priya): finalize perf matrix and send the pilot runbook + acceptance criteria by EOD 6/22.
3) Procurement: we will supply a preliminary reserved throughput quote once the GPU shortlist is confirmed.

I uploaded the initial hypothesis matrix and test plan here: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1A2B3C-acme-perf-matrix and attached a working spreadsheet (priya-acme-matrix.xlsx) with the early numbers. Ben/Karthik — can you review the matrix and add notes on the streaming test harness and cost calc?

Thanks — we'll try to keep the pilot narrowly scoped and time-boxed.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
priya.natarajan@redwood.ai

Attachment: priya-acme-matrix.xlsx (XLSX, 98KB)
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-21T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Re: Thanks + perf targets we discussed

Quick technical notes / clarifications (internal):
- Model details: if the fine-tuned LlamaR variant uses 2-stage decoding or sampling with top-k=40, we should expect slightly higher p95. Need confirmation of sampling settings.
- Sequence length distribution suggests 65% under 512, 30% 512-768, 5% >768. This helps pick a GPU memory profile; H100/A100 preferred for headroom if 1024 hops are frequent.
- Streaming harness: we'll implement a per-token flush test to measure first-byte latency and steady-state per-token latency; include cold-KV and warm-KV runs.
- Warm-up: scalable warm-up job with progressive concurrency ramp (0 -> 8 -> 20) over 30 minutes. We should also record KV hit-rate sensitivity.

I'll add the harness checklist to the shared sheet and include rough run durations per GPU (estimate 6-8 hours / GPU for a full sweep).

—Ben
Ben Carter
Principal Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Jordan Li <jordan.li@acmehealth.com>

Cc: Acme Health Ops <ops@acmehealth.com>, Procurement <procurement@acmehealth.com>

Priya — this looks good. A few quick replies inline: 

- Pilot window: 2027-07-05 to 2027-07-19 works for us.
- SRE POC: Jordan Li (me) and Maya R. (maya.r@acmehealth.com) for day-to-day; Procurement lead is Anil S. (anil.s@acmehealth.com).
- Sampling: our model uses top-p sampling at 0.92, top-k disabled; average tokens emitted per request ~140, total gen ~512.

Please go ahead and send the pilot runbook and the reserved throughput quote once Ben/Karthik finalize the matrix. Can you also include a short appendix with the expected cost delta between H100 and L4 assuming quantization (ballpark only)? Procurement will need that to justify the reserved spend.

Forwarding your plan to Procurement for initial alignment.
